item.title: 【Helpdesk】[HELP] Modern Talking – Brother Louie (1986) – Film Gate Weave / Image Stability Issues
item.description:
Hey everyone!
I've been working on a restoration of Modern Talking – Brother Louie (1986) and was wondering if anyone could help me with an issue I've been struggling to correct.

For this project, I've used a combination of Topaz Video AI's Starlight model to upscale the original music video footage, alongside footage I've sourced from my own Blu-ray copy of the film featured in the video.

The results have been pretty promising so far, but there's one issue that's been bothering me: the image appears to jump or shift slightly between frames, which I believe may be film gate weave or instability introduced during the original transfer.

I'm looking for a way to stabilise these unwanted movements without compromising the original camera motion, framing, or restored image quality.

Here's a sample of my current restoration:

https://pixeldrain.com/d/me/TestBrotherLouie.mp4

Has anyone encountered something similar or managed to correct this kind of instability?

Would something like AviSynth, VapourSynth, DaVinci Resolve, or another restoration tool be able to correct it effectively?

I'm particularly interested in a solution that preserves the original movement rather than relying on AI frame interpolation or excessive cropping.

Any advice, suggestions, or example scripts would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks in advance!

Music / Live Concerts / Singer-Songwriter / Pop-Rock / Latin Music / Full Blu-ray

Recorded live at the Palacio de los Deportes in Madrid during their historic 2007 joint tour across Spain and Latin America spanning 72 concerts, "Dos pájaros de un tiro" (Two Birds with One Stone) brings together on the same stage two absolute legends of Spanish-language music: Joan Manuel Serrat and Joaquín Sabina.
